# WordPress.org plugin directory rules

Source of truth (do not invent policy):

- FAQ: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/plugin-developer-faq/
- Guidelines: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/detailed-plugin-guidelines/
- Block Directory extras: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/block-specific-plugin-guidelines/
- Common issues: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/common-issues/

This repo’s WordPress.org slug, plugin folder, text domain, and GitHub name are **`tocguide`**. Display name: **TOCguide**. After WordPress.org approval the slug cannot change. See `docs/NAMING.md`.

TOCguide ships **admin settings, auto-insert, and a shortcode**, so it is a **Plugin Directory** plugin, not a Block Directory “block-only” plugin. Do not strip wp-admin to chase the Block Directory unless Matt explicitly wants a second, editor-only product.

## Identity (locked at approval)

- **Slug** is generated from `Plugin Name:` in the main PHP file (`TOCguide` → `tocguide`). After approval it **cannot** change.
- Slug = plugin folder = WordPress.org URL = SVN path = **text domain**.
- Display name can change later; slug cannot. Prefer a unique coined brand over `wp-…`, `wordpress-…`, or `…-plugin`.
- Slug: English letters + digits only; no vulgarities; no version numbers; do not start with someone else’s trademark; avoid `wordpress` / `plugin` in the slug.
- Do not begin a display name with another brand (`WooCommerce Improved…`). Add-ons: “Improved Search for WooCommerce”, not “WooCommerce Improved Search”. Woo add-ons start permalinks with `wc-`, not `woo-`.
- Company trademark permission does **not** allow a trademarked permalink. Only the trademark owner may start a slug with that term.
- Text domain is the **literal** `'tocguide'` (never a constant or variable).

## What reviewers reject (avoid these)

- Missing or incomplete `readme.txt`; HTML in the plugin header `Description:`.
- Placeholders, unfinished plugins, or zips over 10MB (no `node_modules`, tests, or unused vendor).
- No `WP_DEBUG` testing; PHP notices; custom copies of WP-bundled JS (jQuery, etc.).
- “Powered by” / credit links on the **front end** unless **opt-in and default off**.
- Phoning home, undisclosed remote calls, tracking without explicit opt-in.
- Trialware / locked features until pay; license-key services that only unlock local code.
- Loading JS/CSS from third-party CDNs (fonts are the usual exception); remote executable code; installing plugins from anywhere but WordPress.org.
- Arbitrary code execution plugins (PHP/JS editors, file managers, AI that executes generated code) — not this product, never add them here.
- Framework/boilerplate/library-only plugins; copies of Core or of another plugin with no meaningful difference.
- Dashboard hijack: undismissible nags, review-begging, ads. Welcome notices must be dismissible and stay dismissed.
- More than **5 tags** in `readme.txt`; competitor tags; keyword stuffing.
- Official logos in banners/icons; unaltered third-party logos.
- Minified JS **without** shipping source or a readme link to the unminified files.
- Zips inside the plugin zip; SVN externals (they are omitted from the download).

## The 18 guidelines (must all hold)

1. GPL-compatible (prefer `GPL-2.0-or-later`); all bundled assets too. Never Envato split-license (CSS/JS/images proprietary) if this plugin is listed on WordPress.org — use 100% GPL. See `docs/marketplace/licensing.md`.
2. Author is responsible for every file and every third-party API’s terms.
3. The Directory copy is the copy users get — keep it current.
4. Human-readable code; document the build (`npm run build`) in the readme/repo.
5. No trialware. Paid extras belong in a **separate** add-on hosted off WordPress.org. Do not cripple the free plugin.
6. SaaS wrappers are OK if documented (terms/privacy). Fake “services” that only check license keys are not.
7. No tracking / external contact without documented, authorized consent.
8. No remote executable code; no off-dotorg updates; no admin iframes for settings.
9. No spam, sockpuppets, fake reviews, illegal/offensive conduct.
10. No forced front-end credits.
11. Admin UI feels like WordPress; nags limited and dismissible.
12. `readme.txt` written for humans; max 5 tags.
13. Use Core-bundled libraries, never a private jQuery/etc.
14. SVN is a **release** repo, not git. Don’t trash-commit.
15. Bump the version for every code release so users get updates.
16. Submit only a complete, installable plugin (no name reservation).
17. Respect trademarks in slug, display name, and artwork.
18. Directory maintainers can close or patch for safety.

## Submission & SVN (when listing)

- Submit at https://wordpress.org/plugins/developers/add/ — one plugin at a time; don’t use alt accounts to queue-jump.
- ZIP < 10MB, Plugin Upload format, production-ready. `Contributors:` must be wordpress.org usernames.
- Contact: `plugins@wordpress.org`. Reply **in the existing review thread**; don’t resubmit unless they say so (3-month timeout is the exception).
- Files live in SVN `trunk/` (readme + main PHP at trunk root, not a nested folder). Releases: `tags/1.0.0` (numbers and dots only). Banner/icon/screenshots in SVN `assets/` (sibling of trunk), **not** inside the plugin. This repo keeps design sources in `.wordpress-org/`.
- `Stable tag` in **trunk** `readme.txt` points at a tag; do not use `trunk` as stable.
- `Tested up to`: current WP or current RC — never a future major you haven’t tested.
- Cosmetic readme/asset edits don’t need a version bump; **code** changes do.
- Changelog: current major + previous major in `readme.txt`; older history in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Plugin goes live on first SVN push — don’t push until ready. Closing is treated as permanent.

## Block Directory vs this plugin

Block Directory plugins: one top-level block, `block.json` required, almost no PHP, **no wp-admin menus/options**, no ads, free to use with no account wall.

TOCguide’s settings page, auto-insert, and shortcode make it **ineligible** for the Block Directory. Keep those features. Still follow Plugin Directory guidelines and use a proper `block.json`.

## Before calling a plugin “ready to submit”

- [ ] Unique slug + matching text domain + matching folder
- [ ] `readme.txt` validates; ≤5 tags; privacy/remote calls disclosed if any
- [ ] Headers complete (no HTML in Description)
- [ ] GPL license declared in file + readme
- [ ] Escaped output, sanitized input, capabilities, nonces
- [ ] No bundled Core JS; assets enqueued
- [ ] Uninstall does not run on deactivate; deletion is opt-in
- [ ] Admin code behind `is_admin()`; notices dismissible
- [ ] Source + build documented; `WP_DEBUG` clean
- [ ] Screenshots described in readme; banners/icons original
